requirements.text: When the user clicks the "Add note" button (id="add", class="add", data-testid="add-note-button"), a new note is created and appended to the document body as a <div> element with the class "note". Inside each note, there is a visible, empty <textarea> (data-testid="note-textarea") for user input. The application supports multiple rapid clicks on the "Add note" button, with each click creating a separate note, each containing its own textarea.

The Notes App must allow users to edit notes with Markdown rendering support. When editing a note, the user interacts with a textarea (data-testid="note-textarea") where they can input or modify Markdown content. As the user types Markdown (e.g., # Heading, **bold**, _italic_, [link](...)), the content is dynamically rendered in the main display area (data-testid="note-main") in real-time, with proper HTML formatting (e.g., **Bold** becomes Bold). The app should handle complex Markdown syntax, ensuring that even invalid Markdown (e.g., unmatched **) does not cause crashes or errors, and instead displays the raw input when the user exits the edit mode by clicking the "Edit" button (data-testid="edit-note-button"). All changes should be reflected immediately in local storage to persist the current state of the note.

The Notes App must allow users to create and manage notes with seamless view and edit functionality. When the app page loads, users can create a new note by clicking the "Add note" button (data-testid="add-note-button"). Upon creation, the note should immediately enter edit mode: the textarea (data-testid="note-textarea") is visible for user input, while the main content area (data-testid="note-main") remains hidden. Users can switch between edit and view modes by clicking the "Edit" button (data-testid="edit-note-button"). In view mode, the main content area becomes visible to display the formatted content, and the textarea is hidden; in edit mode, this behavior is reversed. All changes typed into the textarea should be automatically saved to local storage, preserving the note’s state across sessions.

When the user interacts with the Notes App, they should be able to delete a note by clicking the "Delete" button associated with that note (data-testid="delete-note-button"). Upon clicking this button, the targeted note must be immediately removed from the DOM so it no longer appears on the page, and the corresponding entry must also be removed from localStorage to ensure it is no longer part of the stored notes array.

When the Notes App webpage loads, it must retrieve all saved notes from localStorage and display them accordingly. For each stored note, the app should dynamically create a div element with the class note, which includes a div with the class tools containing an "Edit" button (data-testid="edit-note-button") and a "Delete" button (data-testid="delete-note-button"). Each note must also include a div with the class main (data-testid="note-main") to show the note content, and a textarea (data-testid="note-textarea") for editing. Notes retrieved from localStorage should be rendered with their content displayed in the main div, with the textarea hidden by default. For notes that have no content, the application should instead show the textarea and hide the main div, allowing immediate editing. If localStorage is empty, no notes should be shown. Internally, the notes variable is used to store the array of note content, retrieved using JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('notes')).

reference_cases.title: [Normal] User clicks 'Add note' button to create a new note
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Note Creation
  The user can create a new note by clicking the 'Add note' button, which displays a new note with an empty textarea for input.


  Scenario: [Normal] User clicks 'Add note' button to create a new note
    Given the Notes App page is loaded
    When the user clicks the 'Add note' button with data-testid 'add-note-button'
    Then a new note is displayed on the page
    And the new note contains an empty textarea with data-testid 'note-textarea'
    And the textarea is visible

reference_cases.title: [Edge] User clicks 'Add note' button multiple times quickly
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Note Creation
  The user can create a new note by clicking the 'Add note' button, which displays a new note with an empty textarea for input.


  Scenario: [Edge] User clicks 'Add note' button multiple times quickly
    Given the Notes App page is loaded
    When the user clicks the 'Add note' button with data-testid 'add-note-button' rapidly
    Then multiple new notes are displayed on the page
    And each new note contains an empty textarea with data-testid 'note-textarea'
    And all textareas are visible

reference_cases.title: [Normal] User types Markdown content into the note's textarea
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Markdown Rendering in Notes The application should render the content typed into the textarea of a note in Markdown format in the main display area. Scenario: [Normal] User types Markdown content into the note's textarea Given the Notes App page is loaded And the user clicks the 'Add note' button with data-testid 'add-note-button' to add a new note When the user enters "# Heading" into the textarea with data-testid "note-textarea" And The user clicks the "Edit" button with data-testid "edit-note-button" to exit edit mode Then the main display area with data-testid "note-main" should render "

Heading

"

reference_cases.title: [Edge] User types complex Markdown content into the note's textarea
reference_cases.description: Feature: Markdown Rendering in Notes The application should render the content typed into the textarea of a note in Markdown format in the main display area. Scenario: [Edge] User types complex Markdown content into the note's textarea Given the Notes App page is loaded And a note is present with a textarea having data-testid "note-textarea" When the user enters "**Bold** and _italic_ text with [link](http://example.com)" into the textarea with data-testid "note-textarea" And the user 'Edit' button with data-testid 'edit-note-button' to exit edit mode Then the main display area with data-testid "note-main" should render "Bold and italic text with link"

reference_cases.title: [Error] User types invalid Markdown syntax into the note's textarea
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Markdown Rendering in Notes
  The application should render the content typed into the textarea of a note in Markdown format in the main display area.


Scenario: [Error] User types invalid Markdown syntax into the note's textarea
    Given the Notes App page is loaded
    And the user click the button with data-testid 'add-note-button' to add a new note
    When the user enters "This is not **valid Markdown" into the textarea with data-testid "note-textarea"
    And the user clicks the 'Edit' button with data-testid 'edit-note-button' to exit edit mode
    Then the main display area with data-testid "note-main" should render "This is not **valid Markdown"

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Create a new note and verify it is in edit mode
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Note Editing Functionality
  The application should allow users to create notes that automatically enter edit mode upon creation. Users should be able to toggle between viewing and editing a note using the 'Edit' button.


  Scenario: [Normal] Create a new note and verify it is in edit mode
    Given the Notes App page is loaded
    When the user clicks the "Add note" button with data-testid "add-note-button"
    Then a new note should be created
    And the note's textarea with data-testid "note-textarea" should be visible
    And the note's main content area with data-testid "note-main" should be hidden

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Toggle note from edit mode to view mode
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Note Editing Functionality
  The application should allow users to create notes that automatically enter edit mode upon creation. Users should be able to toggle between viewing and editing a note using the 'Edit' button.


  Scenario: [Normal] Toggle note from edit mode to view mode
    Given the Notes App page is loaded
    And a note is created with text "Sample Note"
    When the user clicks the "Edit" button with data-testid "edit-note-button"
    Then the note's textarea with data-testid "note-textarea" should be hidden
    And the note's main content area with data-testid "note-main" should be visible

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Toggle note from view mode to edit mode
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Note Editing Functionality
  The application should allow users to create notes that automatically enter edit mode upon creation. Users should be able to toggle between viewing and editing a note using the 'Edit' button.


Scenario: [Normal] Toggle note from view mode to edit mode
    Given the Notes App page is loaded
    And a note is created with text "Sample Note"
    And the user clicks the "Edit" button with data-testid "edit-note-button"
    When the user clicks the "Edit" button with data-testid "edit-note-button"
    Then the note's textarea with data-testid "note-textarea" should be visible
    And the note's main content area with data-testid "note-main" should be hidden

reference_cases.title: [Edge] Create a note with empty content and verify edit mode
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Note Editing Functionality
  The application should allow users to create notes that automatically enter edit mode upon creation. Users should be able to toggle between viewing and editing a note using the 'Edit' button.


  Scenario: [Edge] Create a note with empty content and verify edit mode

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Delete a note successfully
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Note Deletion
  The user can delete a note, which removes it from the page and updates localStorage accordingly.


Scenario: [Normal] Delete a note successfully
    Given the Notes App page is loaded
    And a note is created with the text "Sample Note"
    When the user clicks the 'Delete' button with data-testid 'delete-note-button'
    Then the note is removed from the page
    And localStorage does not contain "Sample Note"

reference_cases.title: [Edge] Delete a note when multiple notes are present
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Note Deletion
  The user can delete a note, which removes it from the page and updates localStorage accordingly.


Scenario: [Edge] Delete a note when multiple notes are present
    Given the Notes App page is loaded
    And  multiple notes are created with texts "Note 1", "Note 2", "Note 3"
    When the user clicks the 'Delete' button on the note with text "Note 2"
    Then the note with text "Note 2" is removed from the page
    And localStorage contains "Note 1" and "Note 3" but not "Note 2"

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Display notes from localStorage on page load
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Display stored notes on page load
  The application should retrieve and display any notes stored in localStorage when the page loads.


  Scenario: [Normal] Display notes from localStorage on page load
    Given the localStorage contains notes with values "Note 1" and "Note 2"
    When the user opens the Notes App webpage
    Then the page should display a note with text "Note 1" in a div with data-testid "note-main"
    And the page should display a note with text "Note 2" in a div with data-testid "note-main"

reference_cases.title: [Edge] Display no notes when localStorage is empty
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Display stored notes on page load
  The application should retrieve and display any notes stored in localStorage when the page loads.


  Scenario: [Edge] Display no notes when localStorage is empty
    Given the localStorage is empty
    When the user opens the Notes App webpage
    Then no notes should be displayed on the page
